newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ICRC to aid war displaced in northwest Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: ICRC to aid war displaced in northwest Afghanistan.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross said on Thursday it would start a relief operation in the coming days to feed some 25,000 people displaced by fierce fighting in northwestern Afghanistan.

Spokesman Peter Iseli said the Geneva-based agency would send 1,000 tonnes of food to the refugees near Qala-i-Nau town fleeing fighting between the radical Islamic Taleban militia and its northern opponents along Murghab river in Badghis province.
An ICRC mission just back from the area reported heavy fighting and casualties, Iseli said but gave no details.
Some 4,000 Afghans fleeing the fighting arrived in the western city of Herat, 130 km (80 miles) from Qala-i-Nau earlier this week, he added.
The Taleban, who captured Kabul on September 27, have been attacking forces loyal to Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum and former Herat governor Ismail Khan in Badghis.
Both sides have used heavy weapons and air power in the see-saw battles in which several towns have changed hands.

If the Taleban break through in Badghis, they could advance into Faryab province and threaten Dostum's northern heartland. If they are defeated, Dostum and his allies could threaten Herat, seized by the Taleban in September 1995.
